name: Zebra
intro: A zebra is a wild animal in the horse family. It has black and white stripes.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A zebra looks like a horse with stripes.
It has black and white stripes.
Its skin under the fur is black.
No two zebras have the same stripes.
There are three kinds of zebras.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Zebras live in Africa.
Most zebras live on grassy savannas.
Some zebras live in the mountains.
They walk far to find grass and water.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Zebras are herbivores, so they eat only plants.
They mostly eat grass.
Sometimes they eat leaves, bark, or fruit.
They spend most of the day eating.
Their teeth keep growing their whole life.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby zebra is called a foal.
A foal can stand about 20 minutes after it is born.
A new foal has brown and white stripes.
It learns its mom's stripes, smell, and voice.
It drinks its mom's milk for many months.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Zebras live in groups called herds.
Zebras can sleep standing up.
Zebras help clean each other's fur.
Zebras like to roll in the dust.
Stripes may help keep biting flies away.

vocab.meaning: A big group of animals that live together.
An animal that eats only plants.
A hot, grassy land with a few trees.
